data.narrative:
Impossible Metals is a Seed-stage climate and energy company that has raised $15M to date. The founding team combines deep technical expertise—Oliver Gunasekara brings 30+ years in technology and led ARM's mobile business, while Jason Gillham founded subsea-robotics firms (2G Robotics and Voyis, acquired January 2020) with 18 years of industry experience—alongside sustainability sector leadership from Director Renee Grogan. The broader Climate & Energy sector includes 1 public comparable (LNZA) and 8 private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix, though no tight peer set exists at the same development stage with sufficient datapoints for direct median-based valuation.

Given data constraints, stage-progression analysis is the applicable method. Using the $15M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement yields $37.5M. This method produced the single triangulated datapoint.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $32M to $43M (median $38M), derived from sensitivity around the stage-progression multiplier (±15% range). Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-stage comparables in Climate & Energy, which limits peer-derived validation, and the early-stage nature of the company, which makes revenue or profitability-based approaches inapplicable. The range reflects typical Seed-stage volatility and should be refined with additional market data as the company progresses.
